title: Feature Expansion for Graph Neural Networks
summary: The paper argues that GNN feature spaces are bounded by weight sharing and by limited node-attribute dimensionality, and it analyzes GNNs as non-parametric feature subspaces reweighted by parameters. It proposes feature subspace flattening (independent weights per subspace) plus structural principal components (a truncated SVD of the graph structure matrix) to expand the feature space. The resulting purely linear FE-GNN gives large gains on heterophilic graphs, e.g. Chameleon accuracy 73.33 with FE-GNN (C).

claims.statement: FE-GNN (C) reaches 73.33% accuracy on Chameleon under random 60/20/20 splits.
claims.config_for_value: FE-GNN (C) Chebyshev polynomial, K=3, hidden 64, lr 0.01, weight decay 0.0005, |S|=700 (truncated SVD of normalized adjacency at 94% singular values), column-wise normalization, purely linear (no dropout/activation), Adam, 100 runs
claims.est_compute: 1x NVIDIA 3090, ~4 s/run x 100 runs, ~7 min at fixed config (plus grid search)

claims.statement: FE-GNN (M), the monomial-polynomial variant, reaches 73.26% accuracy on Chameleon.
claims.config_for_value: Same as C1 but monomial polynomial Pk(L)
claims.est_compute: 1x NVIDIA 3090, ~7 min for 100 runs at fixed config

claims.statement: FE-GNN improves average accuracy by 32.0% over the GCN baseline on the three heterophilic datasets.
claims.config_for_value: FE-GNN vs GCN as in Table 2
claims.quote: FE-GNN achieves on average 32.0% improvement on three heterophilic graph datasets than the GCN baseline.

claims.statement: FE-GNN improves average accuracy by 1.1% over ADA-UGNN on the five homophilic datasets.
claims.config_for_value: FE-GNN vs ADA-UGNN as in Table 2
claims.quote: our FE-GNN achieves a 1.1% accuracy improvement on average on 5 homophilic graph datasets.

claims.statement: On Chameleon, truncated-SVD accuracy peaks when the kept singular values reach 94% of the total.
claims.config_for_value: FE-GNN with S built from top-j singular components; r = sum_{j<=i} Vjj / sum_j Vjj

claims.statement: The truncated-SVD preprocessing costs less than 10% of total training time.
claims.config_for_value: SVD computed once as preprocessing; training time measured per run
claims.quote: the SVD time in the total training time is less than 10%

claims.statement: Polynomial order K=3 is sufficient to reach near-optimal FE-GNN accuracy.
claims.config_for_value: FE-GNN with K swept; accuracy vs K
claims.quote: This suggests that order 3 is good enough to achieve near-optimal performance

claims.statement: Removing the structural principal components (w/o S) drops Chameleon accuracy to 61.54%.
claims.table_ref: Table 5 (also Table 13), row w/o S, column Chameleon
claims.config_for_value: FE-GNN(C) without the SWs term; other settings as C1

match_target.why: Cheapest faithful target of the paper's central result: FE-GNN (C) on Chameleon is the headline heterophilic case (limited node attributes + heterophily) where flattening plus structural principal components give the large margin; one fixed config, ~7 min on a single GPU.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: bounded accuracy on a smaller test set (Chameleon 20% test split is ~455 nodes, under 2,000); the paper reports a 95% CI rather than a std, so rule 1 is not triggered.

requirements.stmt: Implement FE-GNN as H = sum_{k=0}^{K} Pk(L_hat) X W^(k) + S Ws, with an independent parameter matrix per feature subspace.
requirements.quote: FE-GNN uses independent parameter matrices W (k) and Ws to reweight each feature subspace

requirements.stmt: Build the structural expansion subspace S from a truncated SVD of the graph structure matrix.
requirements.quote: we propose to construct the expansion subspace using the truncated SVD of the structural matrix

requirements.stmt: Truncate the SVD so the retained singular values account for 94% of the total.
Apply column-wise normalization so each feature-subspace column contributes equally.
requirements.quote: we add a column-wise normalization to ensure that each column of each feature subspace contributes equally

requirements.stmt: Keep the model purely linear: no activation functions and no dropout, only the cross-entropy loss.
requirements.quote: our implementation is purely linear without any deep artifices such as activation functions or dropout

requirements.stmt: Provide both polynomial variants: Chebyshev (FE-GNN (C)) and monomial (FE-GNN (M)).
requirements.quote: FE-GNN uses the Chebyshev or monomial polynomials to construct the feature space

requirements.stmt: For Chameleon use hidden size 64, lr 0.01, weight decay 0.0005, |S|=700, polynomial rank k=3; search k in {0,1,2,3}.
requirements.quote: Ranks k of the polynomial Pk(ˆL): {0, 1, 2, 3}

requirements.stmt: Use random 60%/20%/20% splits, run 100 times over 10 random seeds, and report mean accuracy with a 95% CI.
requirements.quote: random 60%/20%/20% splits and summarize the results of 100 runs

requirements.stmt: Optimize with Adam and early stopping: warmup 50 plus patience 200.
requirements.quote: We employ Adam for optimization and set the early stopping criteria as a warmup of 50 pluses patience of 200

requirements.stmt: Report average accuracy, which the paper equates with micro F1 for this single-label task.
requirements.quote: We report the average accuracy (micro F1 score) in the classification task
